sample_unit: EHR-based clinical prediction tasks (VUMC and MIMIC IV)

links.outcome: AUROC and Brier score of LLMs versus locally trained gradient-boosting ML on same EHR prediction tasks
links.effect: ML AUROC 0.847/0.894 (VUMC/MIMIC) vs GPT-3.5 0.537/0.517 and GPT-4 0.629/0.602; Brier ML 0.134 vs GPT-3.5 0.384 vs GPT-4 0.251 (VUMC).
links.quote: Traditional ML [AUROC: 0.847, 0.894 (VUMC, MIMIC)] substantially outperformed GPT-3.5 (AUROC: 0.537, 0.517) and GPT-4 (AUROC: 0.629, 0.602) (with and without in-context learning) in predictive performance and output probability calibration [Brier Score (ML vs GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4): 0.134 vs 0.384 vs 0.251, 0.042 vs 0.06 vs 0.219)].

links.outcome: Non-fine-tuned general LLM performance on clinical prediction tasks from EHR data
links.effect: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 had near-chance to poor AUROC (0.517-0.629) compared with locally trained ML, showing general LLM capability does not translate to clinical prediction competence.
links.quote: These findings suggest that non-fine-tuned LLMs are less effective and robust than locally trained ML for clinical prediction tasks, but they are improving across releases.

screen.reason: The study empirically benchmarks LLMs vs traditional ML on EHR clinical prediction tasks, explicitly testing the impact of a safeguard/deployment practice: generalizing demographic variables for privacy protection, as well as evaluating fairness across demographic subgroups.
